As a B1 Licensed Aircraft Engineer, you will work closely with a team of engineers and technicians, providing technical expertise for the maintenance and repair of aircraft systems, including the structure, engines, and mechanical systems.

Your key responsibilities will include troubleshooting, performing routine maintenance, and conducting complex inspections to meet both regulatory standards and our operational excellence. If you are a detail-oriented professional with a passion for aviation, this position offers an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Key Responsibilities:: Perform scheduled and unscheduled maintenance tasks on aircraft in accordance with company and regulatory guidelines.
 Troubleshoot and repair aircraft systems, including hydraulic, pneumatic, and mechanical components.
 Conduct pre-flight and post-flight inspections to ensure aircraft safety and compliance.
 Diagnose issues and determine the necessary course of action for repairs or replacements.
 Complete maintenance logs and reports accurately to document all work performed.
 Work closely with flight crews to ensure the timely and safe return of aircraft to service.
 Ensure that all tools, equipment, and facilities used in maintenance are kept in good condition and properly calibrated.
 Supervise and mentor junior maintenance staff and technicians.
 Liaise with regulatory authorities during inspections and audits.
 Stay updated on industry regulations and technology advancements.
Qualifications:: Valid EASA Part 66 B1 License (or equivalent recognized by local aviation authorities).
 Strong knowledge of aircraft systems, including engines, landing gear, airframes, and associated mechanical and hydraulic systems.
 Minimum of 3 years of experience working on aircraft maintenance, repairs, or modifications.
 Experience with both scheduled and unscheduled maintenance.
 Ability to read and interpret technical manuals, blueprints, and engineering drawings.
 Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to safety.
 Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with minimal supervision.
 Excellent communication skills and ability to work as part of a team.
Preferred Qualifications:: EASA Part 66 B1 License or equivalent qualification (e.g., FAA A&P License, CAA B1 License).
 Aircraft Type Ratings on relevant aircraft models (e.g., Airbus, Boeing, Bombardier, etc.).
 Valid Human Factors certification.
 Current EWIS (Electrical Wiring Interconnection System) certificate.
 Fuel Tank Safety certification (Level 1 and 2 preferred).
 Updated training on relevant regulations (Part 145, Part M, etc.).
 Type ratings on multiple aircraft types.
 Experience in both line and base maintenance environments.
 Certification in advanced aircraft systems troubleshooting techniques.

 Brookfield Infrastructure Group is one of Brookfield’s primary operating groups. The Infrastructure Group is one of the world’s largest infrastructure investors, owning and operating critical assets across the transport, utilities, energy, and data infrastructure sectors. The Group operates and manages approximately $262 billion of assets owned through its private funds and publicly listed entity, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners. Our portfolio of assets facilitate the movement and storage of energy, water, freight, passengers and data, and are located in North and South America, Europe and the Asia Pacific regions.  The University of Ottawa (uOttawa) invites applications for a tenure-track Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position in cancer research and/or cell therapy, aligned with the Government of Canada strategic priority area of Health. This position is associated with the Canada Impact+ Research Chair in Next-Generation Translational T Cell Immunotherapies in the Faculty of Medicine, as part of the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada Program (formerly Canada Impact+ Research Chairs Program). 
 We seek candidates whose research program advances the understanding, development, or clinical translation of immune-based therapies for human disease, including cancer and other conditions where immune modulation offers transformative potential. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to, immunology, cellular therapies, synthetic biology, bioengineering, systems biology, computational and AI-enabled approaches or translational medicine. The successful candidate will leverage our established strengths in immunology, cancer research, translational medicine, and biomanufacturing to build an ambitious research program that spans basic and translational biomedical science.
 The Impact+ Emerging Leader will join the Department of Biochemistry, Microbiology and Immunology (BMI) in the Faculty of Medicine , a vibrant and collaborative research environment with internationally recognized strengths in immunology, infection and immunity, cancer biology, molecular medicine, and translational biomedical research. The successful candidate will have opportunities to build strong collaborations across the University of Ottawa, its affiliated research institutes and hospital partners, and a broad network of national and international collaborators. Candidates whose research complements and expands existing departmental expertise, while fostering interdisciplinary partnerships and training the next generation of scientists and clinician-scientists, are particularly encouraged to apply. The University of Ottawa offers a uniquely collaborative ecosystem that supports innovation at the interface of fundamental discovery, technology development, and clinical translation.
 uOttawa is ranked fifth in research intensity in 2025 and is renowned for pioneering discoveries across multiple disciplines. Several of our research centers and institutes rank among the top 100 globally, including the top six in Canada.  
 Located in Canada’s vibrant capital and proud to be the world’s largest bilingual (English and French) university, uOttawa is minutes away from federal and other government institutions, several national agencies, embassies, international organizations, and connected to the thriving high-tech sector. We are committed to building partnerships across Canada and internationally and fostering innovation and knowledge mobilization in areas of significant social and economic impact.  
 About the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders Program   
 The Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada Program is a very prestigious, one-time initiative designed to support universities in attracting world-leading researchers whose work addresses critical national and global challenges. The program also includes Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders awards, a $120M investment to help institutions recruit internationally based early career researchers to Canada.
 The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders award provides $100,000 per year over six years, with the possibility of a six-year funded extension at the same yearly amount, subject to program conditions. 
 T he Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader must be recruited within the same strategic priority area as the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairholder, but the early career researcher (ECR) and the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairholder don't necessarily need to be in the same discipline or research field or be aligned with the same federal research funding agency. The ECR nominees are expected to have an independent program of research, with potential for impact through collaborations with, but not limited to, the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairholders. Institutions may include support for the ECR in their research infrastructure request to the Canada Foundation for Innovation (CFI) through the Impact+ Research Infrastructure fund associated with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair .   
 Eligibility of Candidates:  
 Only candidates who are internationally based (both working and residing outside of Canada) when the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair is accepted are eligible. Candidates who are at uOttawa or are based in Canada are not eligible to apply for this position as stipulated by the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada Program . Candidates must also meet the program’s early career researcher eligibility requirements.      
 * An early career researcher is a researcher within five years from the date of their first independent research-related appointment, minus eligible delays in research, where:
 research-related appointments are defined as those where the individual has the autonomy to conduct research independently (including assistant professor); and
 all eligible leaves (e.g., maternity, parental, medical, bereavement) are credited as twice the amount of time taken, and professional leaves (e.g., training, sabbatical, administrative) are not credited.
 The successful candidate will be expected to begin their full-time tenure-track appointment at uOttawa by July 3, 2027.
 Skills requirements:  
 Education: Ph.D. or equivalent in a field related to biochemistry, microbiology & immunology, cancer research and/or cell therapy (please note that this is a requirement from the institution, and not the program).  
 Research : Candidates should align broadly with one (or more) of the research foci of BMI such as immunology; cell therapies; genetic & developmental biology; cancer biology.

Excellent communication skills in either English or French. Passive knowledge of one’s second Official Language is a requirement for tenure (language coaching is available). English-French bilingualism is an asset.

 Located on the ancestral land of the Algonquin people, uOttawa is committed to ensuring equity, diversity and inclusion in the scholarly and leadership environments of our students, staff and faculty. Accordingly, we strongly encourage applications from individuals from all underrepresented, equity-seeking, rights-seeking populations, including Indigenous peoples, racialized individuals, persons with disabilities, women and individuals from LGBTQ2+ communities, as well as from all qualified candidates with the skills and knowledge to productively implement equity measures that ensure and retain diverse teams and promote inclusive practices for research team members.

 At Acuity Insights, we’re strengthening our accounting operations, improving our systems, and finding better ways to work. We’re looking for an experienced accountant who can take on complex work independently and help us build a stronger, more effective accounting function.
 As our Senior Accountant, you’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, from close and financial reporting to revenue, reconciliations, and audit readiness. You’ll also help strengthen the accuracy and reliability of our financial and business reporting, including recurring revenue metrics, while contributing accounting insights to budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
 You’ll work closely with our Controller and alongside a small accounting team, bringing the judgment to work through complex accounting questions, identify root causes, and see issues through to resolution. Your experience will also help strengthen the team through shared knowledge, guidance, and better ways of working.
 There’s plenty to improve and build. We’re preparing for a new accounting system, exploring automation and AI, and reducing the manual work that slows us down. You’ll have the opportunity to lead meaningful improvements while helping make our accounting processes more reliable and scalable.
 If you enjoy solving complex accounting problems, sharing what you know, and finding better ways to get things done, there’s a lot here for you to contribute.
 Before you apply: This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. We’re hiring for an existing, open position. You’re welcome to use AI thoughtfully when preparing your application and conversations with our team. Just make sure what you share reflects your own experience, thinking, and judgment. During live conversations, please don’t use AI to generate responses unless invited to do so. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 In your first few weeks, you’ll get to know Acuity’s business, current accounting systems, processes, and controls, working alongside our Controller and accounting team to understand how things work today and where we can improve.
 We’re working toward a five-business-day close, and you’ll play an important role in helping us get there.
 Own complex accounting work 
 You’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, including complex journal entries and reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, and audit support. You’ll also review reconciliations and supporting schedules prepared by the team, investigate unusual items, and ensure the close is complete and ready for Controller review.
 When accounting questions are complex or something doesn’t reconcile, you’ll dig into the details, investigate root causes, and use sound judgment to recommend the right path forward. Your work will help us build a faster, more reliable close supported by strong processes and controls.
 Strengthen revenue accounting and reporting 
 You’ll provide senior-level review and oversight of revenue accounting, including revenue recognition, deferred revenue, reconciliations, and related reporting. Working with teammates responsible for invoicing, receivables, and recurring revenue schedules, you’ll connect business activity with accounting records.
 You’ll review accounting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and resolve complex or unusual transactions. You’ll help ensure revenue is recognized appropriately, supporting schedules reconcile to the general ledger, and financial and business reporting is accurate and reliable..
 Turn accounting information into reliable financial insight 
 You’ll help ensure the accounting information behind our financial and business reporting is accurate, consistent, and reliable, including the preparation and reconciliation of recurring revenue metrics.
 You’ll contribute accounting insights and historical context to financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, helping the business make informed decisions. You’ll also support cash management through short-term cash forecasting, cash flow variance analysis, and visibility into upcoming cash requirements.
 Help modernize our accounting systems 
 We’re preparing to move to a new accounting platform. You’ll contribute your accounting expertise to the transition, from defining requirements and improving workflows to data validation, testing, and migration.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful improvements that make our systems and processes more efficient, reliable, and easier to use.
 Improve how Accounting works 
 You’ll look beyond your own responsibilities to identify recurring problems, unnecessary manual work, and opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and use automation or AI thoughtfully.
 You’ll help turn those opportunities into practical improvements, while strengthening documentation, sharing knowledge, and building better coverage across the team.
 The goal is an accounting function that spends less time moving information around and more time on the work where expertise and judgment matter.
 Who You’ll Work With and How
 You’ll report to our Controller and work alongside a small team of accountants. You’ll have meaningful ownership of your work while sharing knowledge, solving problems together, and helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 Accounting connects to almost every part of Acuity, so you’ll work closely with people across the business:
 Your Accounting teammates , to work through complex questions, share expertise, strengthen coverage, and improve how the team works.
 Revenue Operations , to connect contracts, billing, revenue, and the information that supports accurate financial reporting.

 How You’ll Succeed

 Balance judgment with momentum. You respect accounting standards and controls while knowing when to make decisions, move forward, or bring others in.
 Look for better ways of working. Y ou notice unnecessary complexity and manual effort, finding practical opportunities to improve processes, systems, and controls.
 Share what you know. You document your work, offer guidance, and help build stronger knowledge and coverage across Accounting.

 Are comfortable building while doing. You work effectively as processes evolve, bringing structure to your own work while helping strengthen how Accounting operates.

 Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running
 You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to independently own complex work. Your experience will include:
 Independently owning significant areas of month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, working papers, and general ledger accounting.

 Investigating complex accounting questions and discrepancies, applying accounting principles and professional judgment to determine the right path forward.
 Supporting external audits and maintaining strong documentation, controls, and audit readiness.
 Improving accounting processes, workflows, or systems to reduce manual work, strengthen reliability, and make the work more efficient.
 Working independently in evolving environments, knowing when to make decisions, collaborate, or escalate.

 Steps in the Process

 Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.
 Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.

If you have an example of real work you’re proud of and can share, bring it along. It could be a process you’ve improved or a way you’ve used technology, automation, or AI to work more effectively.  Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and improve ways of working, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
 Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.
 Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.
 Life at Acuity Insights
 We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.
 Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.
 Day to day, you can expect:
 High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done.
 Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team.
 Opportunities to share ideas and perspectives that help inform our direction.
 Colleagues who are generous with their expertise, challenge thinking, and learn from one another.
 A culture of curiosity, continuous learning, and thoughtful experimentation, including how we use AI.
 A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness.

 ServiceCentral is hiring Partnership & Growth Associates to win new customers and grow the ones we bring in. You will build real product depth, get hands-on coaching from people who have done this work themselves, and have experienced support in the room when a deal gets complex. What we are looking for in return is drive, curiosity, and a genuine appetite for hitting a number.

 Pipeline generation and conversion

 Sustain consistent, high-volume prospecting activity as the anchor of your week
 Manage and qualify inbound leads with fast, accurate follow-up and correct routing
 Research accounts and stakeholders so outreach is personalised rather than generic
 Run discovery conversations using our qualification framework, and deliver online product demonstrations
 Close new business against a quarterly quota
 Hand off opportunities above your authority to Specialists, Managers, or Directors with full context, and earn sourced-pipeline credit
 Route opportunities on the other platform to your counterpart owner, and earn referral credit
 Account ownership
 Own the full commercial relationship for your assigned portfolio of accounts
 Maintain a defined contact cadence so no owned account drifts without engagement
 Execute standard renewals cleanly and on time
 Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, closing the simple ones and pulling in a Manager or Director on the rest
 Monitor account health signals and flag at-risk relationships early, before they become recoveries
 Execute defined save plays on accounts showing risk
 Onboarding and time to value
 Own commercial handoff and welcome communications that set clear expectations
 Coordinate onboarding with Solutions and Support so customers reach value quickly
 Track time-to-first-value on your accounts and intervene when it slips
 Act on or route expansion signals that surface during onboarding
 Revenue integrity
 Audit subscription billing on your accounts to prevent revenue leakage
 Monitor involuntary churn signals (failed and declined charges) and drive resolution within 24 hours
 Reconcile the billing platform against internal records so MRR reporting is accurate
 Verify plan changes (upgrades, downgrades, cancellations) are executed correctly before a customer notices an error
 Surface systemic billing patterns to your Manager rather than fixing the same problem repeatedly
 Enablement and team support
 Provide day-to-day support on larger accounts held by senior colleagues: routine maintenance, data updates, configuration changes, and low-complexity requests
 Absorb repeatable work so senior capacity stays on new business and strategic pursuits
 Create and maintain customer-facing Knowledge Base and self-service content that drives adoption and reduces inbound volume
 Verify release notes for accuracy and customer clarity before publication
 Support go-to-market materials and campaign content for upsell and cross-sell motions
 Support trade shows and events: booth materials, collateral, demo environment readiness, on-site coordination, and lead capture with follow-up
 Systems discipline
 Keep CRM records complete and current, with a scheduled next action on every open opportunity
 Log activity accurately, because your forecast and your credit both depend on it
 What We Are Looking For
 Commercial drive.  You want to carry a number and you want to beat it.
 Resilience.  High-volume outreach means high-volume rejection. You need to make the next call sound like the first one.
 Coachability.  This tier exists partly to develop you. The people who progress fastest ask for feedback and visibly act on it.
 Process discipline.  You will run recurring operational workflows (billing audits, cadence management, CRM hygiene) that protect revenue. Reliability here is the foundation of customer trust.
 Commercial instinct.  You notice when a routine support question is actually an expansion signal, and you do something about it.
 Clear written communication.  Your emails, customer-facing content, and CRM notes are all read by someone who will judge us on them.
 Customer empathy.  You will handle billing disputes and pricing conversations. Doing that well protects both the relationship and the revenue.
 Curiosity about the platform.  The Associates who become Specialists learned their platform properly, not just the pitch.
 Autonomy and Escalation
 You operate inside a structured playbook with a clear escalation path. Escalation is a strength at this tier, not a weakness.
 Decide yourself:  standard pricing and terms, routine renewals, day-to-day account management within cadence.
 Escalate: 
 Any discount request, however small
 Any at-risk account signal, immediately
 Billing discrepancies above defined thresholds
 Growth opportunities in your accounts that need a Manager or Director, routed with full context
 Requests for non-standard contract terms, service commitments, or SLAs
 Quota and Compensation
 You will carry a quarterly quota weighted heavily toward new business, with expansion and renewal making up the balance. Quota is set from your assigned accounts and territory rather than a generic benchmark, and it ramps across your first two quarters so you are not held to full target while you are still learning.
 Compensation is a competitive base plus variable, with the variable tied to new business won, pipeline quality, and team performance. We will walk you through targets, weightings, and exactly how performance is measured during the interview process.
 Where This Leads
 Associate is the first rung of a four-tier track. Typical progression to  Partnership & Growth Specialist  takes 12 to 24 months.

 Two consecutive quarters at or above quota
 Clean, independent ownership of your named accounts
 Ability to run discovery unsupervised
 Evidence you have informally coached at least one peer

 On-target earnings: $130k CAD  (base ~$50-70k plus variable). Variable is tied to closed-won new business. When our MD or CCO leads the close on an enterprise deal, you share in the win for the pipeline you built and advanced
 Full benefits
 Remote within Canada, with working hours that overlap Eastern Time, where most of our team sits. 
 Some travel expected, predominantly within North America

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Product Platform org - the group that powers product development across Vanta by building the shared foundations that every engineering team builds on top of. This hire will join one of two closely-aligned teams within the org, each working on foundational challenges with company-wide impact.

 

Application Primitives is responsible for the shared, customer-facing platform components that product teams implement across the product: examples include comments, notifications platform, event log infrastructure, and agentic audit trails. This team sits at the intersection of platform and product - not pure infrastructure, not pure product - building the reusable building blocks that let other teams ship faster and more consistently.

 

Libraries & Foundations is a brand-new team that owns Vanta's internal engineering libraries and golden-path patterns. Sitting between core platform and product platform in the stack, this team builds the TypeScript-first abstractions and shared foundations that all Vanta engineers build on top of - including event-driven architecture libraries, code quality tooling, and test frameworks.

 

You'll be evaluated for both teams based on your background and interests, and the decision on team placement will reflect where your skills and passions are the strongest fit.

 

Visit our Vanta Engineering Blog https://www.vanta.com/all-categories/engineering to learn more about what our team is working on! 

 

What you’ll do as a Senior Software Engineer, Product Platform at Vanta:

 - Design and build high-quality, scalable systems and shared libraries that multiple engineering teams depend on - whether that's shared customer-facing components (Applications Primitives) or internal abstractions (Libraries & Foundations)

 -  Partner deeply with product engineering teams to understand their needs and translate them into clean, well-documented APIs and services

 -  Drive technical decisions and influence architecture across team boundaries, with a focus on developer experience and platform scalability

 -  Define and uphold engineering standards for shared components, ensuring consistency, performance, and security across the systems you own

 -  Participate actively in code review, design discussions, and technical planning - raising the engineering quality bar for your team and beyond

 -  Write and maintain thorough documentation for the systems and libraries you build, enabling engineers across the org to use and contribute to them

 - Contribute to building Vanta's engineering culture as we scale

 

How to be successful in this role:

 - Industry experience in backend or fullstack software engineering, with a focus on platform, shared infrastructure, or developer-facing systems

 - Experience building shared APIs, services, or platform components used by multiple engineering teams - a platform mindset is critical

 - Familiarity with distributed systems, event-driven architecture, or message queue systems (Kafka, SQS, pub/sub)

 - Excellent communication skills - able to work cross-functionally with engineering, product, and design stakeholders, and to clearly articulate technical trade-offs

 - Track record of shipping high-quality, maintainable code with sound judgment on architectural decisions

 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

We tackle hard technical problems, own our outcomes, and push for excellence at every level — from architecture to deployment. It's an environment where engineering is a craft, and builders become leaders.
 What you’ll do 
 Travel & Expense is one of the highest-leverage domains at Brex, and it spans several engineering teams — expenses, travel, policy, and spend controls — that have to work as one system for customers. We're looking for a Staff Engineer who operates across all of them. You won't own a single team or service. Your mandate is to find the most important problems across T&E — the ones that fall between teams, the ones nobody is holding — and drive them to a solution.

You'll set technical direction across the group, raise the bar in design and review, and be a force multiplier for the engineers and EMs you work alongside. You'll partner closely with our existing Staff Engineers as peers, and you'll have a seat at the T&E leadership table to help shape where the org invests.  Partner as a peer with existing Staff Engineers and with EMs across expenses, travel, policy, and spend controls to align on direction and unblock execution.

 We are seeking an experienced Automotive Service Technician (310S) or skilled automotive technician with professional shop experience to join our collision repair operation.
 We are primarily an EV-focused collision repair facility , working extensively with electric vehicles and the systems, components, and repair procedures associated with modern EV platforms. The successful candidate will receive ongoing exposure and training in EV repair and diagnostics as part of their role.
 This position offers an opportunity to play an important role in our mechanical operations, with a primary focus on mechanical inspection, diagnosis, and repair of collision-damaged vehicles .
 As part of the continued development of our business, we are also establishing a dedicated mechanical service offering from our existing collision repair facility. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to perform general mechanical repairs and service work for local customers while supporting the mechanical requirements of our collision operation.
 We are looking for an experienced, dependable technician who takes pride in their work, has strong diagnostic ability, and is interested in developing their skills in both conventional and electric vehicle repair.
 Position Responsibilities
 The primary focus of this position will be the mechanical assessment and repair of vehicles involved in collisions.
 Responsibilities will include:
 Performing mechanical inspections of collision-damaged vehicles
 Identifying steering, suspension, drivetrain, braking, cooling, HVAC, and other mechanical damage resulting from collisions
 Identifying hidden or secondary mechanical damage that may not be immediately visible
 Performing pre-repair and post-repair mechanical inspections
 Removing and replacing suspension components, control arms, knuckles, wheel bearings, steering components, subframes, and related assemblies
 Performing wheel alignments and interpreting alignment measurements
 Assisting with engine, transmission, drive-unit, and drivetrain removal when required for collision repairs
 Performing cooling system and A/C repairs related to collision damage
 Performing A/C recovery, vacuum, and recharge procedures
 Performing mechanical diagnostic scans and basic electrical diagnosis
 Inspecting wiring, connectors, sensors, harnesses, grounds, and component mounting locations for collision-related damage
 Assisting with ADAS-related mechanical preparation and calibration procedures
 Following OEM repair information and manufacturer repair procedures
 Accurately documenting inspection findings and additional damage
 Completing post-repair mechanical inspections and quality-control checks
 Road testing vehicles when appropriate
 Maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work area
 EV Training & Exposure
 As an EV-focused collision repair facility , electric vehicles are a significant part of our daily operations.
 The successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop practical knowledge and experience working with EV systems and repair procedures, including exposure to:
 EV-specific mechanical systems
 Electric drive units and related components
 High-voltage vehicle systems and safety procedures
 EV cooling and thermal management systems
 EV-specific diagnostic procedures and scan tools
 Electrical and electronic systems
 OEM EV repair procedures
 EV-specific collision damage assessment
 Pre- and post-repair scanning
 ADAS and vehicle electronics
 Previous EV experience is an asset, but it is not required. We recognize that EV technology is a developing area of the automotive industry and will provide appropriate training and hands-on exposure to help the successful candidate develop these skills.

 In addition to collision-related mechanical work, this position will support the development of a general mechanical service operation within our existing facility.

 Diagnostic services
 Wheel alignments
 Cooling system repairs
 A/C service and repair
 Electrical diagnosis

 EV and hybrid service and repair as appropriate

 Candidates should have:

 The ability to inspect a vehicle and accurately determine required repairs
 Strong attention to detail

 Experience in any of the following areas would be considered an asset:

 EV diagnostic equipment
 ADAS systems and calibration

The Role
 At Treewalk, you'll run the day-to-day finance engine for the Indigenous governments, organizations and businesses we serve: clean books, a disciplined month-end close, timely funder reporting and year-end files that sail through audit. You'll own a portfolio of clients, acting as their fractional controller. Some will lean on you to keep operations running smoothly month to month; others will need you to get a backlog cleaned up and audit-ready. Either way, every file is yours to run.
 Deadlines are real; overtime isn't a lifestyle. We staff sensibly, treat extra hours as the rare exception, and back that up with true schedule autonomy and remote flexibility, so your evenings stay yours.
 If you've managed controllership or audit-prep engagements at a small- to mid-size firm, or run finance operations inside a First Nation, Tribal Council or Indigenous organization, and you're ready for high-impact work, tangible ownership and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you.
 How You'll Create Impact Day-to-Day
 •         Run a disciplined close – Lead month-end and year-end close across your portfolio: reconciliations, accruals, deferred revenue, capital assets and journal entries, on time and review-ready.
 •         Keep operations humming – Oversee AP, AR, payroll and cash management processes, and step in hands-on when a client needs a fractional controller's precision and speed.
 •         Make audits painless – Build year-end audit files and lead schedules, prep airtight support, clear PBC lists and quarterback conversations with external auditors so leadership can sleep at night.
 •         Get the hard files back on track – Clean up backlogs and prior-year issues, so clients go from catch-up mode to a clean, audit-ready position.
 •         Run the engine of multi-entity groups – Keep the books straight across Nations' governments, economic development corporations, limited partnerships, trusts and societies, including intercompany and fund accounting.
 •         Keep funding on track – Track funding by program, manage deferred and restricted funds, and prepare reporting for ISC, CIRNAC, FNHA and other funders.
 •         Build strong controls – Design practical processes, internal controls and financial policies that hold up to auditor and funder scrutiny.
 •         Grow the team – Coach and review the work of accountants, bookkeepers and CPA students, and build checklists and templates that scale across clients.
 Result: clients see you as the calm, trusted voice who keeps their books clean, their funders satisfied and their audits uneventful, while you build deep, meaningful expertise without the grind of traditional public practice. 
 Our ideal candidate...
 •         CPA designation required.
 •         Significant experience in controllership, month-end close and year-end audit preparation, ideally with Indigenous governments, organizations or not-for-profits.
 •         Strong working knowledge of PSAS / ASNPO, fund accounting and funding agreement reporting.
 •         Experience leading engagements and supervising staff.
 •         A respectful, relationship-based approach and an understanding of Indigenous histories, governance and the impacts of colonization.
 •         After the base experience requirements are met, we hire first and foremost strong analytical thinkers and problem solvers.
 Please mention these bonus skills if you have them
 •         Audit experience at a firm serving First Nations or public-sector clients
 •         Cloud accounting and payroll systems (e.g., QuickBooks Online, Sage, Xero)
 •         FMB Financial Administration Law or certification experience
 •         Lived experience as a First Nations, Métis or Inuit person, or connection to Indigenous communities
 Why Treewalk Feels Different
 It's Treewalk for a reason: we invest in your growth, trust your judgment, and protect your life outside the ledger.
 •         No-Strings Learning Fund – We pay 100% of your CPA modules, annual dues, and any pro-dev courses you choose, and we'll never claw it back if you move on.
 •         Freedom Over Face-Time – Own your deadlines, shape your schedule. Hit a midday workout, do the school run; just bring the results.
 •         Day-One Peace of Mind – Extended health, dental, vision, and parental-leave benefits start the moment you join.
 Who We Are
 Treewalk is Vancouver-born and scaling nationwide. Our Indigenous Services group runs the finance operations of Nations and Indigenous organizations and gets them audit-ready, so leadership can focus on their community's goals while we keep the numbers strong.
 But labels like "accounting firm" don't capture our DNA. Picture a tech startup powered by CPAs:
 •         Holacracy over hierarchy – Ideas outrank titles, and ownership lives on every desk.
 •         Relationships first – We earn trust over the long term and work in a way that respects each community's priorities and protocols.
 •         Growth at warp speed – One of Canada's fastest-rising advisory practices, we set audacious goals, then sprint past them.
 •         Training ground for tomorrow's leaders – Whether you're two years post-designation or a seasoned finance lead, Treewalk is where accountants level up.
 The Values That Power Us
 Mastery: We hunt knowledge relentlessly and build expertise into every engagement.
 Support: No one goes it alone; collaboration is our default setting.
 Ownership: We celebrate wins and own slip-ups with equal conviction.
 Kaizen: Continuous improvement isn't a buzzword; it's our daily operating system.

 We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Management to build and lead the operating infrastructure required to bring our products to market, scale them globally, and support them throughout their lifecycle. This role sits within the Supply Chain organization and reports to the Sr. Director, Operations & Strategic Partnerships. This role has high exposure to CEO level decisions and engagement and demonstrated leadership experience is a requirement.
 This is a builder role within the Supply Chain. You will own the Supply Chain deliverables covering our cross functional go to market and customer engagement. This includes driving product certifications and market readiness, enhancing RMA and customer satisfaction processes, as well as driving our Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Your job is to establish clear ownership, build scalable processes, develop the team, and create the operating mechanisms required to support a rapidly growing hardware business, working in close partnership with the other functions needed to achieve these goals.
 We are not looking for someone to administer existing processes. We are looking for someone who sees ambiguity, creates structure, drives decisions, and most importantly takes end-to-end ownership. Your mandate is simple: build it, own it, and scale it.
 This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON; Austin, TX; or Santa Clara, CA. 
 We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.
 Who You Are 
 A builder who is comfortable entering an environment where processes and ownership are not fully defined, then turning ambiguity into a clear operating model and an executable plan.
 An experienced hardware and supply chain operator who understands how Engineering, Product, Sales, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, Legal, and customer teams connect across the product lifecycle.
 A cross-functional leader who can align senior stakeholders, establish decision rights, and drive accountability without waiting for someone else to define ownership.
 A data-driven and analytically rigorous decision-maker who can make sound judgments with incomplete information and maintain urgency through execution.
 A people leader who develops strong teams, builds subject matter expertise, and creates a culture of ownership, transparency, and continuous improvement.

 Drive cross-functional processes and own Supply Chain deliverables for global product certification and market readiness, including certification roadmaps across products and countries, clear readiness gates, coordination with Engineering, Product, Legal, manufacturing partners, test labs, and regulatory bodies, and early mitigation of risks that could affect customer commitments or launches.
 Own and mature the company’s S&OP process by connecting customer demand, Sales forecasts, supply, manufacturing capacity, inventory, and financial objectives into a disciplined operating cadence and trusted view for executive decision-making.
 Build and own the end-to-end global RMA and customer operations model within Supply Chain, covering intake, triage, replacement, repair, warranty management, disposition, customer communication, service levels, escalation paths, and performance metrics, in partnership with Customer, Quality, and Engineering teams.
 Establish the processes, systems, KPIs, dashboards, governance, and operating mechanisms required to scale, including measures for forecast accuracy, supply performance, inventory health, backlog, certification readiness, RMA performance, and execution against plan.
 Lead cross-functional execution with Sales, Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Manufacturing, test labs, regulatory bodies, and customer teams.  Gain broad exposure to the full operating model of a rapidly growing hardware and semiconductor business, from product development and global market readiness through supply planning, manufacturing, delivery, and customer support.
 Build expertise in integrating Supply Chain-owned certification deliverables, S&OP, RMA, and customer operations into one scalable product lifecycle operating system.
 Develop the leadership and operating mechanisms required to turn cross-functional complexity into clear ownership, timely decisions, and measurable execution.

Functionally reports to Extrusion Team Lead. Responsible for optimally operating the press, process equipment, handling equipment and die setup in a safe and efficient manner. Responsible for following Company policies and procedures by ensuring a safe working environment is maintained at all times.  We believe that every Employee is responsible to act safely and to model good safety practices.
 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The duties and responsibilities of the Press Operator are detailed below, but not limited to the following:
 Efficiently operate the extrusion press while maintaining good quality that meets Almag’s quality standards. 
 Keep track of equipment performance and ensure press is well tuned, and temperatures are being properly managed from billet oven to press exit temperatures.
 Responsible for monitoring runout efficiency such as length, speed, and finish.
 Reference work orders to ensure press is running at the optimal speeds to maximize productivity.
 Ensure billet zone temperatures are setup, monitored and maintained throughout the runs. Mark extrusions accordingly if temperatures do not meet requirements.
 Die management - Ensure all necessary tooling is available at the beginning and throughout shift.
 Load dies into press and ensure presses are not waiting for die changes. Importance must be given to ensure dies are not loaded too early or too late.
 Ensure die temperatures are maintained when dies are loaded and removed from the ovens.
 Responsible for communicating directly with the team leads/maintenance team if any mechanical breakdowns or issues are encountered.
 Ensure proper billets/logs are in the ovens and monitor the supply to keep press going.
 Ensure average speeds are followed based on information contained on work orders. If deviations occur, ensure note is made in EPICS and Team Lead is notified.
 Responsible for EPICS entries for billet lengths, cut offs, cut sizes, etc., and highlight any special notes and instructions that the team needs to focus on. 
 Responsible for entering all downtime, die fails, quality issues, and schedule adherence notes in EPICS.
 Responsible for checking notes in EPICS and viewing drawings throughout the shift to ensure work orders are followed correctly.
 Responsible for checking the run out on the second billet produced. Report to Team Lead if billet length scheduled is inappropriate and have it changed to improve yield.
 Ensure sufficient spacing is kept between extrusion pieces on the cooling table to make sure proper cooling is maintained.
 Responsible for ensuring the extrusion is correctly fed into puller jaws. Notify maintenance/team lead if any issues occur.
 Ensure exit/runout temperatures are monitored and maintained throughout the run. 
 Maintain quality checks at front end of press during operation and continuously throughout the shift.
 Press samples must be properly labelled and kept together for traceability
 Ensure samples are taken after the first billet and verify dimensions and surface finish according to drawings in EPICS.
 Ensure all billets and alloys used are accounted for in EPICS and documented accurately.
 Check finish and dimensions on extrusions at the required frequency.
 Complete press Ascona scans as required.
 Must have knowledge and ability to operate all equipment at saw and stretcher.
 Other duties as assigned. 
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 
 Education/Experience 
 High school Diploma with some technical background and mechanical aptitude.
 Extrusion experience is an asset.
 Technical Skills/Competence 
 1-2 years’ experience in an industrial environment.
 Knowledge of machinery and ability to read drawings is an asset. Willing to train.  
 Must be willing and able to train and develop as a saw operator / inspector, stretcher operator and die preparation operator as understating these jobs and their impact is critical to developing as a competent press operator.
 Basic computer skills including MS Windows is required. Other MS software is an asset. 
 Understanding of measurements, tolerances, basic geometry, and numeracy comprehension.
 Ability to lift up-to 50lbs independently, and ability to lift up-to 100lbs in collaboration with a team member.
 Familiarity with extrusion software such as EPICS is an asset.

ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and deliver production-grade AI agents https://sierra.ai/blog/meet-the-ai-agent-engineer: You'll build and ship highly performant, reliable, and intuitive AI agents that are central, mission-critical and drive revenue directly to Sierra's growth. These aren't prototypes—they are powerful, scalable systems running in production environments across industries like finance, healthcare, and commerce.

 - Drive the Agent Development Life Cycle https://sierra.ai/blog/agent-development-life-cycle (ADLC): You'll have complete ownership and autonomy from initial pilot through deployment and continuous iteration. You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

 - Partner with large enterprises and cutting-edge startups: You’ll work directly with leaders at some of the world’s largest enterprises to understand their most pressing business challenges, and build AI agents that transform how they operate at scale. You'll also partner with the most cutting-edge startups in Silicon Valley, embedding AI agents across their entire business stack to drive innovation and efficiency.

 - Build the future of the platform: Your direct work with customers will guide the evolution of Sierra's core platform. You'll surface unmet needs, prototype new tools and features, and collaborate with research, product, and platform to shape the future of AI agent development and Sierra's product.


EXAMPLE PROJECTS

These are some examples of projects that engineers on our team have worked on recently:

 - Design and build AI agents for large telecommunications and media companies that consistently outperform human agents in managing subscription churn

 - Develop and refine AI agents capable of navigating complex customer interactions, like troubleshooting a broken device and personalizing product recommendations

 - Create generalizable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog https://sierra.ai/blog/five-ways-to-use-ai-agents-financial-services!

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Language fluency - professional fluency in both Spanish and English

 - Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems

 - Strong technical problem-solving skills, especially in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

 - A builder and tinkerer’s mindset with high agency - you find creative ways to overcome obstacles and ship

OUR VALUES

veritree and Job Overview
 veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.
 veritree is seeking an Product Marketing Manager to own the commercialization of our restoration portfolio: turning every project we plant into a sales-ready package, and acting as the technical and impact expert our revenue teams bring into the room.
 We have active restoration projects across the globe, each one carries real depth, identifying the purpose behind the site, whether the trees are permanent or on a managed harvest rotation, the species mix and why it was chosen, survivability and monitoring data, the workers and communities involved, and the ecosystem returning around it. We need someone who can translate project details into one canonical source of truth, packaging it into narratives, value propositions, and assets our Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success teams can actually use, and then standing behind it on live calls.
 This role is a deliberate blend of product marketing, product ownership, and sales enablement. You will own the story of what we sell, not the marketing gloss, but the substantive, verifiable, layered version that wins enterprise deals. This is a storyteller's role first. You will be fluent enough in forestry, permanence, survivability, and our on-site technology to hold your own with a sustainability lead or a diligence team, but the reason we're hiring is narrative craft: the ability to make a Fortune 500 buyer feel what changes for a worker who once felled trees for income and now earns more, more securely, planting them.
 12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)
 Source of truth, live and trusted. One canonical project library covering 100% of active projects — purpose, permanence and harvest model, species mix, survivability, monitoring methodology, workforce and community context, ecosystem outcomes — current, maintained on an agreed cadence with Forest, and surfaced in internal materials for live call support.
 Every project sales-ready. A sales-ready package shipped for every active project: positioning, value proposition, proof points, pricing guidance, and customer-facing assets. No rep builds their own version from scratch.
 Impact story, three layers deep. A worker, community, and ecosystem narrative built and evidenced for our priority projects, backed by real data and media from veritree's technology — credible enough to survive diligence, specific enough to be memorable, and never greenwashing.
 Enablement that changes rep behaviour. Playbooks, proof-point libraries, objection handling, and training delivered so every Account Executive, Business Development Rep, and Customer Success Manager tells the same story, with adoption measured through call reviews and certification rather than assumed.
 Launch discipline. A cross-functional launch checklist and readiness standard, owned by you and adopted across Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, so nothing goes to market half-built.
 What You'll Do
 Source of Truth & Project Intelligence 
 You will build and own veritree's canonical library of project facts — one current, authoritative reference for every project we sell, replacing the scattered documents and tribal knowledge in use today.
 You will work directly with the Forest team to turn their intake into commercially usable intelligence: project purpose, permanence versus managed harvest and rotation length, species selection and rationale, survivability and mortality data, monitoring methodology, and site-level context.
 You will keep it current, with a defined maintenance cadence, clear ownership of each input, and version control the rest of the business can rely on.
 You will make it accessible where our teams actually work, surfacing project facts in Forge and our AI tooling so a rep can get an accurate answer during a live call, not after it.
 Packaging, Positioning & Pricing 
 You will translate every project into a sales-ready package: the narrative, the value proposition, the proof points, and the per-project assets that make it sellable.
 You will standardize delivery into ecosystem packages — mangrove, terrestrial, wildfire, agroforestry — rather than rebuild bespoke every deal, and you will own the product catalogue.
 You will own positioning across our growing solution portfolio, so that as we move from selling a single product toward solution-selling across multiple offerings and stakeholders, the story stays coherent.
 You will partner with Revenue and Finance on per-project pricing guidance and the commercial logic behind it, ensuring reps understand not just the price but why the project is worth it.
 You will own the change-flow when a metric is updated. When survivability, planting hours, or carbon updates, you push the correction into collateral, the portal, and CS on a set cadence — and you audit what's already in market.
 You will define which projects we lead with for which segments, and build the matching logic that helps reps put the right project in front of the right buyer.
 Impact Storytelling 
 You will build the impact narrative at three layers, and go deeper than the category norm on each:
 The worker — what this work actually changes for the individual, including the person who once cut and sold timber to feed their family and now earns better, more secure income restoring the same landscape.
 The community — how stable, better-paying restoration work compounds into local economic resilience, and what that looks like in the specific communities we operate in.
 The ecosystem — what returns to the site: canopy, soil, water, birds, wildlife, biodiversity — and how our technology measures and verifies it.
 You will ground every layer in evidence, using veritree's existing monitoring technology, field data, and media to turn claims into proof our clients can publish and defend.
 You will partner with Marketing to convert that depth into case studies, impact reports, campaign material, and event content.
 Sales Enablement 
 You will turn Forest's methodologies into sales-ready material — survivability, planting hours, social impact, carbon, permanence, verification — as defensible talk tracks, proof points, and objection handling. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one, and you only ever ship the defensible one.
 You will own the enablement library for project and impact content: playbooks, proof points, objection handling, discovery guidance, and competitive framing.
 You will design and deliver training and certification so every rep across Business Development, Sales, and Customer Success can tell the story consistently and credibly.
 You will review calls, identify where the story is breaking down, and close the gap with better material and better coaching rather than more documents.
 You will run a feedback loop from the field back into packaging, so what we ship next reflects what actually lands with buyers.
 Expert Support on Live Calls 
 You will act as the on-call project and impact expert, joining sales and Customer Success calls to explain projects in depth to prospects and customers when a rep needs the specialist in the room.
 You will handle the questions reps can't: permanence and additionality, survivability and replanting, harvest rotation and end use, monitoring and verification methodology, species and site selection, social impact measurement.
 You will represent veritree credibly in front of sustainability, ESG, and procurement stakeholders, and support diligence when deals require it.
 You will treat every call as a diagnostic. The goal is not to be permanently required on calls — it is to notice what reps couldn't answer and turn that into material and coaching so they can next time.
 You will not own the deal, carry a quota, or run the commercial conversation. The rep owns the deal; you make the rep formidable.
 Project & Product Launch 
 You will own the launch checklist and cross-functional readiness for new projects and new solutions — the definition of "ready to sell" and the gate that enforces it.
 You will own each project's availability, not just its launch — taking it online when it's ready and offline when it's sold out or paused.
 You will coordinate Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success through launch, so readiness is planned rather than scrambled.
 You will own the internal communication of what's new: what changed, what it means commercially, and what each team needs to do about it.
 Cross-Functional Partnership 
 You will sit at the seam between Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success, and you will be the person all of them come to for the truth about a project.
 You will feed field and buyer insight back to Forest and Product, influencing which projects we source, how we describe them, and what our technology needs to capture next.
 Requirements 
 Professional Requirements
 Exceptional storytelling and writing ability. This is the core of the role. You can hold a room, and you can put the same idea on a page without it going flat. We will ask for writing samples and we will read them closely.
 5-8+ years in product marketing, brand or content strategy, communications, or a comparable narrative-led role. Adjacent backgrounds are welcome — journalism, documentary, impact communications, science communication — if you can show the commercial application.
 A track record of packaging complex or technical subject matter into positioning, narratives, and assets that a sales team actually adopted — with evidence of adoption, not just delivery.
 Demonstrated sales enablement experience — building playbooks, proof-point libraries, and training programs, and measuring whether they changed rep behaviour.
 Comfort being customer-facing as the subject-matter expert: you can present with authority to an enterprise audience and hold up under informed questioning, without needing to run the commercial conversation.
 Genuine appetite for technical and scientific subject matter, and the discipline to represent it accurately. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one. You do not need a forestry background — you need to be the kind of person who will go and learn it properly.
 Experience owning cross-functional process — launch checklists, readiness gates, intake-to-market workflows — in an environment where that process didn't exist yet.
 Fluency with CRM and enablement tooling (HubSpot preferred) and a builder's instinct for using AI to make knowledge accessible at the point of need.
 Based in or able to work core hours in the PST time zone, and willing to travel to customer sites, planting sites, and the Vancouver office as required.
 Personal Strengths
 A storyteller by instinct — you notice the specific detail that makes an abstract claim land, and you reach for it before the statistic.
 A builder who is comfortable creating structure, systems, and process where none exists.
 Genuinely curious about the substance — the forestry, the science, the communities — not just the pitch.
 Mission-driven, with real conviction about restoration done credibly and a low tolerance for greenwashing.
 Rigorous and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know which details matter to a buyer and which don't.
 Influences without authority: you can get Forest, Product, Marketing, and Sales moving in the same direction without owning any of them.
 Clear, direct, and calm under pressure — tech-forward and credible, never cliché.
 Nice to Haves (not mandatory)
 Experience in tree planting, forestry, carbon markets, sustainability, or nature-based solutions.
 Familiarity with ESG and nature reporting frameworks (CSRD, TNFD, SBTi, CDP).
 Experience with MRV (measurement, reporting, and verification) methodologies, remote sensing, or field data collection technology.
 Background in social impact measurement or community development.
 Experience building AI-assisted knowledge bases or enablement tooling for live call support.
 Benefits 
 Why This Role
 You will own the story of what veritree actually sells — and at a company whose entire premise is verified impact, that story is the product. It is a rare brief: real material to work with, twenty-plus projects and the people and ecosystems inside them, plus the data to prove every word of it. You will have the autonomy to build a function that doesn't exist yet, the access to go deep on projects most people only ever see as a line item, and the mandate to make sure the way we sell restoration is as rigorous as the way we deliver it.
 Benefits & Compensation Overview
 At veritree, we recognize that compensation and performance development are key to attracting and retaining top talent. Our approach is grounded in fairness, transparency, and creating opportunities for growth as both our people and business scale.
 Some highlights you can expect include:
 Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth.
 Extended health, dental, and vision benefits.
 Additional Health Spending Account (HSA) / Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) to support your well-being and lifestyle interests.
 A variety of time-off programs, including vacation, personal days, and a 4-week remote work program each year.
 Employee discount with tentree, our sister company.
 A flexible, hybrid work environment designed for collaboration and focus-driven impact.
 veritree ensures that compensation is reviewed fairly and consistently, with opportunities for salary progression tied to sustained performance. As such, the salary range for this role including variable compensation is $93,544 to $108,186 CAD.
 This range is positioned around the 50th-75th percentile of market data we've collected, reflecting our commitment to competitive pay. Final offer amounts are based on the individual experience and skillset of the candidate demonstrated during the recruitment process.
 We reserve the >75th percentile of our salary ranges for internal employees who demonstrate sustained high performance and impact at veritree.
 veritree is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business needs.

Please note that this posting is not tied to an immediate vacancy. We are proactively building a pipeline of qualified candidates in anticipation of potential hiring needs over the coming months. Applications will be reviewed and retained for future consideration as opportunities arise.
 We are seeking a Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help support the execution of lighting work across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on production role with opportunities to take on project-level leadership responsibilities. In addition to completing assigned lighting work, you may help coordinate tasks, review the work of other artists, provide constructive feedback, and ensure scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios to translate creative direction into lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, and performance.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, lighting pipeline, gameplay requirements, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, and other project disciplines.
 Create polished lighting work that meets the project’s established visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for assigned scenes, environments, sequences, or gameplay areas.
 Provide useful feedback and support to other artists when asked to review or coordinate lighting work.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and communicate them to the appropriate project leads.
 Deliver assigned work on schedule and respond effectively to internal and client feedback.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.
 Maintain visual consistency across related environments, gameplay spaces, sequences, times of day, and lighting conditions.
 Bring assigned scenes from initial lighting setup through final polish.
 Respond to feedback from Art Direction, project leadership, and clients in a timely and professional manner.
 Ensure completed work meets project requirements for quality, performance, organization, and delivery.
 Leadership and Quality Support
 Help oversee lighting work for an assigned scene, group of scenes, feature, or milestone when requested by project leadership.
 Review the work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting.
 Provide clear, respectful, and actionable feedback through written notes, live reviews, reference images, paintovers, or in-engine examples.
 Help ensure lighting work follows approved visual targets, technical standards, and project requirements.
 Communicate expected outcomes, priorities, and quality standards to artists working within an assigned area.
 Monitor the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that may require additional revision or support.
 Confirm that feedback has been addressed before work is submitted for senior, Art Director, or client review.
 Support junior or less-experienced artists with lighting fundamentals, engine workflows, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.
 Lead by example through reliable execution, clear communication, constructive collaboration, and professional conduct.
 Escalate unresolved quality, schedule, scope, or technical concerns to the appropriate senior artist, Art Director, or Producer.
 Planning and Production Support
 Work with Art Direction and Production to understand lighting priorities, tasks, estimates, and milestone expectations.
 Help break lighting goals into clear and manageable production tasks.
 Provide progress updates and communicate when assigned work is at risk of missing quality, technical, or scheduling requirements.
 Participate in daily reviews, art reviews, milestone evaluations, and planning discussions.
 Help prepare lighting work for internal reviews, client presentations, milestone submissions, and final delivery.
 Balance hands-on production responsibilities with review, coordination, troubleshooting, and team support.
 Adjust priorities when creative direction, technical requirements, production scope, or client feedback changes.
 Maintain accurate task status and documentation using the project’s production-management tools.
 Technical and Pipeline Responsibilities
 Work with Technical Art and Engineering to ensure lighting is visually effective, technically stable, and appropriate for the target platform.
 Follow established budgets for dynamic lights, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, global illumination, memory, and scalability.
 Identify and help resolve issues involving exposure, shadow artifacts, light leaking, reflections, volumetrics, bake quality, material response, and post-processing.
 Use dynamic, baked, stationary, or hybrid lighting approaches according to the project’s established pipeline.
 Profile assigned lighting work and make informed visual adjustments to meet performance requirements.
 Validate lighting across relevant gameplay cameras, display settings, hardware targets, times of day, weather states, and scalability levels.
 Follow project standards for scene organization, naming conventions, source control, documentation, and asset integration.
 Contribute to reusable lighting setups, templates, documentation, validation processes, and team best practices.
 Identify workflow problems and communicate potential improvements to senior artists, Technical Art, or project leadership.
 Cross-Discipline Collaboration
 Collaborate with Environment Art to ensure geometry, materials, composition, and set dressing support the intended lighting.
 Partner with VFX to integrate fog, particles, weather, fire, emissive effects, and atmospheric elements.
 Work with Design to ensure lighting supports navigation, player guidance, combat readability, objectives, and interactive systems.
 Coordinate with Character Art and Animation to maintain readable and appealing character presentation.
 Support cinematic lighting needs involving shot composition, continuity, exposure, character lighting, and narrative focus.
 Communicate artistic and technical concerns clearly to both creative and non-creative stakeholders.
 Work effectively with distributed teams, partner studios, external vendors, and clients across different time zones.
 Requirements
 Professional experience creating lighting for games, real-time projects, animation, visualization, or a closely related field.
 A portfolio or reel demonstrating strong real-time lighting work.
 Strong understanding of lighting fundamentals, including value, color, contrast, composition, visual hierarchy, atmosphere, exposure, shadow, and material response.
 Experience lighting gameplay environments or interactive real-time scenes.
 Understanding of how lighting supports mood, gameplay readability, navigation, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Professional experience using Unreal Engine or another modern real-time engine.
 Experience with dynamic or baked lighting, global illumination, reflections, volumetrics, exposure, color grading, and post-processing.
 Working knowledge of physically based rendering and material response.
 Understanding of basic lighting optimization, including light cost, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, scalability, and platform constraints.
 Ability to take ownership of assigned scenes and follow them through review and completion.
 Ability to receive, interpret, and implement artistic and technical feedback.
 Experience reviewing artwork or providing constructive feedback to teammates.
 Ability to identify work that does not meet an established quality target and communicate practical improvements.
 Ability to balance visual quality, technical requirements, production scope, and schedule.
 Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
 Ability to organize priorities, communicate risks, and follow work through to completion.
 Experience collaborating with multiple game-development disciplines.

 Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a distributed team.
 Tools and Technical Experience
