 Unreal Engine 5 or another modern real-time engine
 Lumen or comparable real-time global-illumination systems
 GPU Lightmass, CPU Lightmass, or comparable baked-lighting systems
 Real-time profiling, visualization, and debugging tools
 Photoshop or comparable image-editing software
 DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, After Effects, or comparable color and compositing tools
 Maya, Blender, 3ds Max, or another 3D content-creation package
 Perforce or another production source-control system
 Jira, Confluence, Miro, or comparable planning and documentation tools
 Expertise with every listed application is not required. We are primarily interested in candidates who demonstrate strong lighting fundamentals, sound production judgment, adaptability, and the ability to learn project-specific tools.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience working in co-development, outsourcing, consulting, or work-for-hire game production.
 Experience contributing to a shipped PC or console title.
 Experience working across realistic and stylized visual pipelines.
 Previous experience acting as a lighting point person, task coordinator, reviewer, or feature owner.
 Experience guiding junior artists or supporting teammates without formal management authority.
 Experience working with remote teams, partner studios, or external vendors.
 Experience owning lighting for a level, environment, sequence, or gameplay feature.
 Knowledge of Unreal Engine systems such as Lumen, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, volumetric fog, reflection systems, exposure controls, post-process volumes, and scalability settings.
 Experience with dynamic time-of-day systems, weather systems, destructible environments, or changing gameplay states.
 Experience lighting cinematics, characters, dialogue scenes, or scripted sequences.
 Knowledge of cinematography, photography, film lighting, camera exposure, and color theory.
 Familiarity with HDR displays, tone mapping, calibration, or accessibility considerations.
 Familiarity with rendering pipelines, shader behavior, and material development.
 Familiarity with Blueprints, Python, editor scripting, automation, or technical-art workflows.
 Experience creating lighting documentation, templates, benchmark scenes, or review materials.
 Portfolio Requirements
 Your portfolio or reel should demonstrate:
 Strong real-time lighting with effective composition, mood, color, contrast, readability, atmosphere, and scene cohesion.
 Work presented in a commercial, proprietary, or modern real-time engine.
 Clear explanations of your individual contribution, responsibilities, workflow, and production decisions.
 Gameplay lighting that guides attention, supports navigation, and reinforces the intended player experience.
 Effective integration between lighting, environments, materials, VFX, atmosphere, characters, and post-processing.
 An understanding of optimization, scalability, technical limitations, and production constraints.
 Examples showing ownership of lighting from initial setup through final delivery.
 The ability to work from concept art, reference, environment blockouts, narrative direction, gameplay requirements, or developing creative direction.
 Adaptability across different projects, genres, visual styles, or lighting conditions.
 We also encourage applicants to include:
 Day and night treatments of the same environment.
 Dynamic and baked lighting examples.
 Lighting created for different gameplay states, weather conditions, or times of day.
 Before-and-after comparisons showing how lighting improved readability, mood, composition, or performance.
 Examples of work reviewed or coordinated under your guidance, with your responsibilities clearly explained.
 Lighting guides, reference boards, benchmark scenes, review notes, documentation, or templates created for teammates.
 Please clearly identify your individual contribution to collaborative work.
 How to Apply
 A resume and portfolio or reel link are required.
 Please include shipped-game credits or comparable professional project experience where applicable. Candidates may be asked to participate in a portfolio review, technical discussion, leadership interview, or art assessment as part of the selection process.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

This role is for a highly experienced Back-End Software Engineer who wants to work on core systems that shape how the platform (Model Vault) operates. You will help define the architecture of the platform where reliability, security, performance, and simplicity all matter, and where many of the problems do not have off-the-shelf solutions.

Model Vault is Cohere’s inference platform for deploying and operating models securely at enterprise scale. The team owns the systems between a customer and the underlying AI infrastructure, including identity, deployments, metering, billing, security, privacy, and confidential computing. We are strengthening these systems as Model Vault grows, with the goal of scaling to millions of users and supporting some of the world’s most demanding enterprise workloads.



AS A SENIOR/STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL:

 - Evolve and scale the backend systems that power Model Vault, including authentication and authorization, deployment management, billing, metering, and customer lifecycle.

 - Lead major architectural initiatives across identity, payments, usage systems, platform scalability, and other core product foundations.

 - Build highly reliable control-plane services for provisioning, configuring, scaling, and operating model deployments across clouds and hardware platforms.

 - Design APIs and distributed systems with strong guarantees around correctness, consistency, isolation, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.

 - Build security and privacy into the platform architecture, including tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditability, secrets management, encryption, and confidential computing boundaries.

 - Solve complex problems that span backend systems, cloud infrastructure, security, and AI inference, where conventional SaaS patterns are often not enough.

 - Drive projects end-to-end, from architecture and threat modeling through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration based on real customer workloads.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - You are a strong backend engineer with excellent fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, networking, operating systems, and security.

 - You have strong programming fundamentals and experience building production systems in languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, or similar. You write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and make thoughtful tradeoffs between simplicity, performance, and correctness.

 - You have designed and operated production systems where correctness, availability, security, and performance mattered at significant scale.

 - You can take ambiguous, high-impact technical problems, define the right architecture, and drive them through to reliable production systems.

 - You have strong systems-design instincts and understand concepts such as concurrency, consistency, caching, queues, rate limiting, backpressure, failure domains, idempotency, and graceful degradation.

 - You think deeply about security boundaries and understand authentication, authorization, identity, cryptography, secrets, tenant isolation, and how small implementation choices can create significant security risks.

 - You are comfortable reasoning across backend services, APIs, databases, distributed systems, and the cloud infrastructure they run on.

 - You are comfortable diving into unfamiliar codebases and debugging complex problems that cross service or system boundaries.

 - You care about the details of production engineering, including instrumentation, capacity planning, migrations, backwards compatibility, incident response, and safe rollouts.

 - You are comfortable challenging existing architecture and evolving foundational components when the system’s needs change.

 - You have a track record of taking technically difficult projects from an unclear starting point to systems that other engineers and customers depend on.

ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.
We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.
 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.
 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.
 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
 Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards
 SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS
 Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:
 Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
 Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
 Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
 Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
 Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
 Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.
 Professional Experience 
 8+ years of experience across nonprofit fundraising/development, development strategy and/or development operations, including at least 5 years working directly within nonprofit or philanthropic fundraising. Candidates must demonstrate a deep practical understanding of the fundraising cycle, funder decision-making, proposal development and stewardship.
 Strong track record leading the development of complex philanthropic/grant proposals, ideally involving multiple programmes, geographies or internal stakeholders.
 Demonstrated experience turning frontline or field-level input into strategy and prioritization. 
 Demonstrated people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, setting priorities and allocating team capacity. Experience leading a distributed team is strongly preferred.
 Experience operating in a global or matrix organisation, with demonstrated ability to influence and coordinate country leaders, programme teams and other stakeholders who do not report directly to them.
 Comfortable using CRM and pipeline data to support fundraising decisions, forecasting and team management.
 Familiarity with the climate, clean energy, or entrepreneurship support landscape is a strong plus.
 Experience conducting dedicated funder-market or landscape research is advantageous.
 Personal Attributes 
 Structured, analytical thinker who is comfortable synthesizing messy, qualitative field input into clear recommendations.
 High level of adaptability in an environment with evolving team structures and workflows, with a genuine comfort operating in ambiguity - this means being a self-starter and embodying a growth mindset.
 High emotional intelligence — able to lead and support a development team well, build trust with country leads across diverse cultural contexts, and approach unfamiliar markets and norms with genuine curiosity and cultural sensitivity.
 Exceptional written communication skills — able to distill complex, multi-market fundraising intelligence into concise strategy and proposals.
 Strong project management skills; able to run a coordination function across concurrent proposals, deadlines, and stakeholders.
 Comfortable being an internal partner and "connective tissue" role rather than the primary external face of fundraising.
 Ability to work with a global team across time zones, with periodic travel for internal team meetings and relevant conferences/convenings.
 Proficiency in database/CRM management, Google Workspace, and Slack.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Foundational knowledge of global clean energy and climate change solutions and ecosystems and willingness to engage in in-depth self-learning on any gaps.
 Experience building or adding structure to a development operations function from an earlier, more informal stage.
 Due to the global nature of the organization and team, some meetings will take place outside of regular work hours.

 This is a full-time remote position. Relocation assistance is not available for this role and compensation is competitive for the market the candidate is based in. Applicable benefits such as medical, dental, vision, paid time off, paid holidays and insurance will depend on the location of the selected candidate.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 Role Overview 
 AI is rapidly changing how software is designed, built, tested, reviewed, deployed, and operated — and the industry playbook is being rewritten monthly. Okta's Developer Productivity and AI Enablement Engineering teams own building and operating the capabilities that make our engineers fast across the inner and outer development loops. This role is the product counterpart, embedded full-time with that organization, that makes those investments compound by uncovering and prioritizing frictions, bringing the outside in, driving standardize-vs-federate decisions, spreading what works across teams, funding and clearing the path for the best tools, and proving the value.
 We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to own developer productivity as a product across Okta's development lifecycle — AI-native and traditional tooling alike. You will start bottom-up: interviewing engineers, managers, tech leads, and architects; mapping current inner- and outer-loop tooling and the frictions; and baselining dev-cycle metrics. From there, you will own the roadmap with engineering leadership; benchmark how the best engineering organizations build with AI; define tooling requirements and/or run the tooling evaluations engineering needs in a landscape that changes monthly; find the teams inside Okta getting outsized results and turn their patterns into playbooks; lead build, buy, integrate, and standardize decisions, including the vision for reducing implementation diversity across Okta and Auth0; clear the security, legal, procurement, and budget paths that slow adoption; and own the measurement that connects investment to engineering outcomes — evidence engineering leaders can take into any room.
 This is a highly technical internal platform role that creates value for Okta through a cross-team, cross-industry, cross-functional layer that turns individual wins into organizational capability.
 What You'll Do 
 Product Strategy & Discovery: Own the vision, PRDs, and prioritized backlog for Okta's internal developer productivity and AI tooling. Treat engineers as your customers: start with deep, bottom-up discovery (dozens of engineer, EM, tech lead, and architect interviews), baseline dev-cycle metrics, and secure tooling budgets with rigorous, ROI-driven business cases.
 Ecosystem Validation (Build vs. Buy): Drive definitive "adopt, build, or pass" decisions. Run hands-on, structured evaluations of inner- and outer-loop tooling — from coding agents and MCPs to build, CI/CD, and code review systems — against strict security and TCO criteria to ensure internal investments amplify vendor capabilities.
 Hands-On Execution: Embed full-time with Developer Productivity Engineering and own the roadmap jointly with its engineering leads. Define MVP scopes, manage sprints, and incrementally ship workflows. You own the strategy and requirements (the what and why); Engineering owns the technical execution (the how).
 Adoption & Outcomes: Own org-wide adoption, clearing security, legal, and privacy hurdles along the way. Measure success by connecting tool usage directly to hard engineering outcomes (cycle time, quality, toil reduction).
 Standardization & Lighthouses: Coordinate the vision for reducing implementation diversity across Okta and Auth0 engineering. Study high-performing teams to see who is getting exceptional results, and convert those patterns into scalable playbooks that shift the broader org from passive AI use to agentic workflows.
 What We're Looking For 
 5+ years of product management experience with developer platforms, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or AI products.
 Experience owning internal or platform products where users have alternatives — adoption driven through product quality rather than mandate.
 Strong understanding of modern software development workflows — source control, IDEs, CI/CD, testing, code review, observability, production operations — across the inner and outer loops of development.
 Hands-on, current fluency with AI-assisted software development — coding agents, context management, MCP, evaluation frameworks — and informed views on where these tools create leverage and where they introduce risk.
 Demonstrated ability to design and run technology evaluations and controlled experiments, and to define measurement systems for developer productivity with judgment about their failure modes.
 Ability to engage credibly in technical and architectural discussions with senior engineers while maintaining clear boundaries between product outcomes and engineering implementation.
 Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across engineering, security, architecture, and finance without direct authority.
 Excellent written communication in a docs-first culture; you can produce solid action plans from incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous inputs.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience deploying or scaling developer tools across a large, multi-org engineering organization — including consolidating divergent stacks and the change management that comes with it.
 Hands-on familiarity with developer AI tools, harnesses, APIs, MCPs, and agent orchestration frameworks.
 Familiarity with developer productivity research (DORA, SPACE, DX Core 4) and its failure modes.
 Experience establishing governance, evaluation frameworks, or spend management for rapidly evolving, consumption-priced technologies.
 Why This Role Matters 
 AI-assisted development is becoming both one of the largest levers on engineering velocity and one of the largest new variable costs in R&D. The playbook changes monthly, and the organizations that win are the ones that learn fastest from the outside, spread what works internally, and measure honestly. That learning-and-leverage layer doesn't build itself — engineering teams optimizing locally, however well, still leave organizational value uncaptured and accumulate divergent implementations that slow everyone down.
 This role exists to capture it: dedicated product leadership that brings engineering the external intelligence, funded tooling, cleared paths, shared patterns, and defensible evidence to build with AI faster than any single team could alone — while deepening Okta's firsthand credibility as the company that secures the AI-powered enterprise for its customers.

 Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

 L’équipe des applications de fabrication numérique de Pratt & Whitney est à la recherche d’une personne très motivée, autonome et proactive, qui souhaite contribuer à la mise en œuvre de solutions numériques au sein de notre plateforme d’entreprise MES et MOM afin de soutenir nos centres moteurs partout dans le monde.  Assurer la liaison entre les processus d’affaires et les fonctionnalités et capacités du système MES.

 Soutenir l’intégration avec d’autres solutions d’entreprise.
 Collaborer avec les clients internes, les fournisseurs externes et les partenaires d’affaires afin de concevoir et de développer des solutions systèmes répondant aux exigences, en tirant parti des technologies les plus récentes.

 Travailler simultanément sur plusieurs projets et produire régulièrement des rapports d’avancement dans le cadre d’un processus d’approbation par étapes.

 Please note that this posting is not tied to an immediate vacancy. We are proactively building a pipeline of qualified candidates in anticipation of potential hiring needs over the coming months. Applications will be reviewed and retained for future consideration as opportunities arise.
 We are looking for an Environment Artist / Generalist with strong hands-on art skills, solid technical judgment, and the potential to grow into broader lead responsibilities over time.
 This role is ideal for someone who enjoys both creating high-quality 3D art and helping teams work more clearly, consistently, and efficiently. Depending on the project, this person may contribute directly to asset creation, world building, scene assembly, feedback, task breakdowns, workflow documentation, quality reviews, and cross-studio collaboration.
 Because our projects can vary widely in style, scope, platform, and client needs, we are looking for an adaptable artist with a strong art eye, a practical production mindset, and the ability to help translate creative direction into actionable work for other artists.
 This is a hands-on production role with opportunities to support team alignment, mentor other artists, improve workflows, and grow toward lead-level responsibilities.
 This role offers flexible work options, including remote, hybrid or in-office arrangements.
 Responsibilities
 Create high-quality 3D environment art, props, modular assets, materials, set dressing, and world-building content across a variety of visual styles.
 Work from concept art, reference, style guides, blockouts, client direction, or incomplete/vague creative briefs to produce clear and polished results.
 Build, assemble, and integrate assets and environments in Unreal Engine, with attention to composition, readability, performance, and technical requirements.
 Support the full environment art pipeline, including modeling, UVs, baking, texturing, material creation, optimization, engine integration, and final polish.
 Review artwork from internal teammates, partner studios, or external vendors and provide clear, constructive, actionable feedback.
 Help translate broad client or project feedback into specific tasks, priorities, notes, and acceptance criteria that artists can execute against.
 Assist with maintaining visual consistency across assets, scenes, and artists by helping define quality bars, style expectations, and review standards.
 Collaborate with art directors, leads, producers, technical artists, designers, engineers, and artists across multiple studios and time zones.
 Help identify production risks early, including unclear direction, workflow gaps, quality issues, technical constraints, or schedule concerns.
 Contribute to workflow and pipeline improvements that help the team work more efficiently and consistently.
 Document processes, best practices, feedback, and workflow guidance when needed using tools such as Confluence, Miro, or Jira.
 Balance visual quality, production efficiency, and performance requirements while supporting the needs of each project.
 Requirements
 5+ years of professional experience as a 3D Environment Artist, Generalist, World Artist, or similar role in games or real-time production.
 At least one shipped game or comparable real-time interactive project.
 Strong portfolio demonstrating high-quality environment art, world building, prop creation, materials, and/or scene assembly.
 Strong artistic eye for form, composition, lighting, material definition, scale, visual hierarchy, and style consistency.
 Ability to work across different visual styles, from realistic to stylized, depending on project needs.
 Experience creating both individual assets and assembled environments/scenes.
 Solid understanding of the full environment art pipeline, including modeling, UV layout, baking, texturing, materials, optimization, and engine implementation.
 Professional experience with Unreal Engine.
 Proficiency with common production tools such as Maya, Blender, ZBrush, Substance Painter, Substance Designer, Photoshop.
 Practical understanding of real-time performance considerations, including LODs, draw calls, texel density, texture memory, collision, lightmaps, shaders/material complexity, scene organization, and asset budgets.
 Strong communication skills, especially when giving feedback, clarifying direction, documenting decisions, or breaking down complex problems.
 Ability to take vague or high-level direction and turn it into clear, actionable work.
 Comfortable collaborating with artists, leads, producers, and cross-discipline partners.
 Able to give and receive feedback professionally, clearly, and constructively.
 Strong ownership, follow-through, and problem-solving ability.
 Interest in growing into broader leadership responsibilities over time.
 Nice to Have
 Previous experience mentoring artists, reviewing work, or informally supporting lead-level responsibilities.
 Experience working with outsourcing, co-development, partner studios, or external vendors.
 Experience collaborating with teams across different countries, cultures, and time zones.
 Experience providing feedback through written notes, paintovers, drawovers, video reviews, live calls, or structured review documents.
 Proficiency with common production tools such as Perforce, Jira, Miro, and Confluence.
 Experience helping define style guides, quality bars, workflow documentation, or art review standards.
 Experience breaking down client feedback into Jira tasks, art notes, production plans, or acceptance criteria.
 Experience with procedural workflows, Houdini, Blueprint, Python, scripting, or tool-assisted content creation.
 Experience with optimization passes, performance profiling, memory budgets, or platform-specific art constraints.
 Experience with both realistic and stylized production art.
 Experience in multiple engines or real-time pipelines.
 Experience working directly with clients or helping support client-facing reviews.
 Portfolio Requirements
 Please include a portfolio that clearly demonstrates your environment art and/or generalist capabilities.
 Strong portfolios should include:
 Finished 3D environments, scenes, props, or world-building examples.
 Examples rendered or captured in a real-time engine, preferably Unreal Engine.
 Breakdowns showing your process, including blockout, modeling, UVs, baking, texturing, materials, set dressing, lighting, and final integration where applicable.
 Examples that show your ability to work across different visual styles.
 Examples of modular kits, reusable asset systems, material workflows, or production-friendly environment pipelines.
 Any examples that show technical problem solving, optimization, performance-aware decisions, or efficient workflows.
 If showing team-created work, please clearly explain what you personally contributed.
 Nice to have: examples of feedback, mentorship, documentation, workflow improvements, style matching, or before/after improvements you helped guide.
 Nice to have: written context explaining the goal of the work, constraints, tools used, your role, and any production challenges you helped solve.
 Candidate Profile
 The ideal candidate is not just a strong artist, but someone who naturally thinks about how the whole team succeeds.
 You may be a great fit if you:
 Care about making great-looking art and making the process better for the team.
 Enjoy solving production problems, not just completing assigned assets.
 Can look at a scene or asset and identify what is working, what is not, and how to improve it.
 Communicate feedback in a way that is clear, respectful, and useful.
 Can help artists understand not just what to change, but why it matters.
 Are comfortable adapting to different clients, art styles, pipelines, and project needs.
 Have the judgment to balance quality, speed, technical constraints, and team bandwidth.
 Are interested in growing toward lead responsibilities while remaining hands-on in production.
 How to apply
 Resume + portfolio link required.
 An art test may be required as part of the process.

 Ce rôle est idéal pour une personne adorant créer de l’art 3D de haute qualité et aider les équipes à travailler de manière plus claire, cohérence et efficace. En fonction du projet, cette personne pourrait contribuer directement à la création de ressources, à la construction de mondes, à l’assemblage de scènes, aux commentaires, à la décomposition des tâches, à la documentation des flux des travaux, aux contrôles de qualité et à la collaboration entre les studios.

 Responsabilités
 Créer des environnements 3D de haute qualité, des accessoires, des ressources modulaires, des matériaux, des décors et du contenu de création de monde dans une variété de styles visuels.
 Travailler à partir de concepts artistiques, de références, de guides de style, de maquettes, de directives client ou de briefs créatifs incomplets ou vagues pour produire des résultats clairs et peaufinés.
 Créer, assembler et intégrer des ressources et des environnements dans Unreal Engine, en accordant une attention particulière à la composition, à la lisibilité, aux performances et aux exigences techniques.
 Prendre en charge l’intégralité du processus de création artistique des environnements, incluant la modélisation, les UV, le « baking », la texturation, la création de matériaux, l’optimisation, l’intégration dans le moteur et le peaufinage final.

 Aider à maintenir la cohérence visuelle entre les ressources, les scènes et les artistes en aidant à définir les seuils de qualité, les attentes en matière de style et les normes de révision.
 Collaborer avec des directeurs artistiques, des chefs d'équipe, des producteurs, des artistes techniques, des concepteurs, des ingénieurs et des artistes issus de différents studios et fuseaux horaires.
 Aider à identifier les risques de production tôt dans le processus, incluant les directives imprécises, les lacunes dans les flux des travaux, les problèmes de qualité, les contraintes techniques ou les préoccupations en matière d’échéancier.

 Capacité à travailler avec différents styles visuels, du réaliste au stylisé, selon les besoins du projet.

 Excellentes compétences en communication, surtout pour fournir des commentaires, clarifier les directives, documenter les décisions ou décomposer les problèmes complexes.

 Atouts
